data.name: Nicanor
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'nika' meaning victory and 'nor' meaning power or strength. In Greek mythology, Nicanor was a warrior who fought in the Trojan War and was known for his bravery. In Christian tradition, Saint Nicanor is remembered for his devotion and faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the triumph of faith and courage over adversity.

in_hebrew.name: ניקנור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ניקנור מורכב מ'ניק' שפירושו נצחון ו'נור' שפירושו אור או אל, לכן ניתן לפרש את השם ניקנור כ'נצחון עם האל' או 'אור הנצחון'. השם ניקנור מוזכר בברית החדשה ובמספר מקורות יהודיים ומשקף תכונות של נצחון וגדלות.

in_greek.name: Νικάνωρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Νικάνωρ προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'νίκη' που σημαίνει νίκη και 'άνωρ' που σημαίνει άνθρωπος. Συνεπώς, το Νικάνωρ σημαίνει 'νικητής άνθρωπος' ή 'άνθρωπος της νίκης'. Στο πλαίσιο της χριστιανικής παράδοσης, το όνομα Νικάνωρ συνδέεται με την έννοια της πνευματικής νίκης και της ανδρείας.

in_latin.name: Nicanor
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Nicanor is derived from the Greek words 'nike' meaning victory and 'anōr' meaning man. Hence, Nicanor can be interpreted as 'victory of God' or 'God's victorious one'. In Christian tradition, the name Nicanor signifies spiritual triumph and devotion to divine will.

in_english.name: Nicanor
in_english.meaning: Victory of God or God's victorious one
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicanor originates from Greek roots, combining 'nike' (victory) and 'anōr' (man). It signifies 'victory of God' or 'God's victorious one'. In Christian tradition, Nicanor is associated with spiritual victory, courage, and devotion. The name appears in the New Testament and is linked to early Christian martyrs and saints.

biblical_reference.note: Nicanor was one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles in the early Christian church.

saint_reference.note: Saint Nicanor is recognized as one of the seventy disciples of Jesus Christ and is venerated in the Roman Catholic Church and Eastern Orthodox Church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nicanor emerged during the Hellenistic period, where it was a common name among the Greeks. However, with the spread of Christianity, the name took on a new significance as it became associated with Saint Nicanor, a deacon in the early Christian Church who was known for his bravery and dedication to the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Nicanor represents the powerful victory that comes through faith and devotion. It serves as a reminder of the strength and courage that comes from trusting in God and following His will. The name can also be seen as a reminder of the victory that will be achieved in the afterlife through faith in Jesus Christ.

historical_references.reference: According to 2 Maccabees 15:23, Nicanor was a Syrian-Greek general who led the Seleucid army against Judah Maccabeus in 160 BC. He was defeated and killed at the Battle of Adasa.
historical_references.context: Part of the Hasmonean Revolt against the Seleucid Empire

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, there is a mention of a certain Nicanor in the Book of Acts (5:5-6), described as a 'receiver of tithes' who died after being rebuked by the apostle Gamaliel. No specific time period is given, but it is generally believed to be in the late 1st century AD.
historical_references.context: A member of the Jewish Sanhedrin

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nicanor has its origins in the ancient Greek language and is of biblical origin, as it appears in the Old Testament as the name of a Syrian general who led an army against the Jewish people. In modern times, the name has gained popularity as a unique and meaningful choice for baby names. On platforms such as Babynames.com, Quora.com, and Wikipedia.com, Nicanor is often discussed in the context of its ancient roots and mythological associations. Some modern parents may be drawn to the name for its historical significance and unique sound, while others may be interested in the mythological figure Nicanor from Greek mythology. In general, Nicanor is considered to be a rare and interesting name, and its ancient origins and biblical associations give it a rich and meaningful backstory that can appeal to parents looking for a name with a strong cultural heritage.

name_in_real_life.story: John Nicanor from New York, United States embodies the meaning of Nicanor - "Conquering or victorious". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicanor in Greek means "victorious" or "conqueror." In a spiritual context, this name represents a strong and unwavering faith in God, who grants us the strength to overcome challenges and emerge victorious in life's battles. It is a reminder that with God by our side, we can conquer any obstacle.
